records.derivation: Pre-flight requirement (Science Concept Review slide 'Requirements – Ambient Environment', dated May 4, 2014), not a statement about the tests as run. The text layer flattens the exponent: '10-5g0' is printed as 10 to the power -5 times g0 (the same requirement is written '1x10−5 as the required g-level (g0 is the earth normal gravity)' in the SRD). Not a measured g-level for the CFI tests.

Hot and Cool-Flame Combustion of N-dodecane Droplets at Moderately High Pressures in Microgravity, 34th Annual Technical Meeting, The American Society for Gravitational and Space Research, 31 October – 03 November, 2018, Rockville, Maryland.
records.derivation: Title of a 2018 presentation listed under the CFI Final Report appendix '6c. Presentations' (post-flight; CFI flew Jan-Sep 2017 per page 4). Its subject (n-dodecane droplets, elevated pressure) matches the CFI test matrix (page 6: 'Pure n-dodecane at 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 2, 3, and 5 atm'), but the title is a citation, not a sentence stating that the CFI tests were run in microgravity, and the cited presentation itself is not in the corpus.

not_found.looked_in: No sentence in the past tense saying the CFI tests themselves were burned in microgravity / low gravity. Searched (page index pages.jsonl lines 6732-6897 + record dump): record JSON (all sections: hypothesis and researchImpacts only state aims; projectType 'Microgravity Investigation' is a label); Final Report pages 1-13 (page 4 'CFI experiments were conducted onboard the ISS from January 2017 through September 2017' = platform only; page 6 rationale already held as R1; page 3 and page 5 'in microgravity' sentences are about FLEX/FLEX-2); SCR pages 1, 3-17 (page 3 'cool-flame burning in microgravity observed for the first time' is a FLEX summary; page 4 objective 'by conducting droplet combustion experiments in low gravity' is the same pre-flight objective as held R3, not repeated; page 5 'Justification for Long-Duration Microgravity' is rationale; page 8 g-level requirement proposed as R701; page 16 'Require measurement of g-level during experiment' has no value); SRD pages 1-54 (page 14 'Examination of the SAMS data showed that the g-levels (across the frequency spectrum) were typically less than 10−5g0' is past tense and measured, but it is in SRD section 2.3 describing the FLEX tests 'reported herein' in a 2014 document written before CFI flew, so it is NOT proposed for CFI (would be analogy, rule 7); pages 30-33 objective/justification already held as R3); Operational Requirements and Protocols page 1 (no gravity term); presentation 'Aspects of Cool-Flame...' pages 1-19 (2015, FLEX results; title only); presentation 'Cool Flames in Space...' pages 1-24 (2013, FLEX; page 23 already held as R101); DataSummary spreadsheet sheets Master Sheet/DATA/Camera Settings/Igniter/Comments/Graphs (no gravity term; Comments describe droplet drift only); experimental table CSV rows 1-25 shown in index (no gravity column); Analyzed Data FLEX-1206..FLEX-1393 summary plots (labels only). SCR page 2 is absent from the page index (not inspected: PDF renderer unavailable). No normal-gravity (1-g) CFI comparison tests found. Terms: microgravity, micro-gravity, low gravity, low-gravity, reduced gravity, g-level, g0, weightless, in space, buoyan*, spherically symmetric.

lineage: CFI (PSI-39) uses the FLEX hardware (MDCA in the CIR): Final Report page 6, 'The experimental hardware is same as that of the FLEX experiments with few minor modifications in the data acquisition systems.' CFI test ids are FLEX numbers (FLEX-1206 to FLEX-1431, Final Report page 7), shared with FLEX/FLEX-2 (PSI-68/69). The only measured g-level sentence in the PSI-39 folder (SRD page 14, 'typically less than 10−5g0') belongs to the FLEX tests described in the 2014 SRD, not to CFI. Saffire-I, -II, -III (PSI-98/99/100) share one flight-unit design and one 'SAFFIRE Objectives, Development and Status' paper filed under all three accessions (Objectives page 5: 'The decision to develop flight units of nearly identical design').
